name: Erosion 20
notes: Flaked paint as a coverage family: level N = N% of the film REMAINING, so the ladder runs from a few surviving flakes (10) to craquelure with a few lost chips (90). One cellular survival field (tips/erosion.spec.json: three Worley scales of per-cell random values + a clustering fbm - a dip along the coarsest cell walls) thresholded at nine NESTED levels: paint only ever disappears as the level drops, so the family is one surface progressively flaking. Whole cells drop at once, which is what makes the chips angular - a Gaussian field cannot do this (phase, docs/fractal-texture-math.md par.4) - and the wall dip keeps the crack lines below threshold at high coverage. Dual-gate train as oil-sponge; AA at 0.45 canvas px because a paint film breaks sharply. Audited comb-free and isotropic. Flake clusters survive in patches; the substrate has won.
